title: Add bounded gate runner orchestrator/gate.py and [gate] config
spec:
What: a new module orchestrator/gate.py that runs the repo gate (.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh) under a hard timeout, plus a [gate] table in .orchestrator/pool.toml. Nothing calls it yet; a dependent task wires the daemon, merge and flaky-rerun paths onto it.
Why: in luna-inbox tests-green runs hung for 6 h (xcodebuild on the simulator) with no timeout; daemon.py:1448 and merge.py:57 call subprocess.run with no timeout, and failures.py:152 uses subprocess.run(timeout=...) which kills only the direct child, leaving xcodebuild/node/simulator children alive.

Interface contract (exact names; the dependent task codes against these):
- DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 2700; KILL_GRACE_S = 15
- settings(cfg=None) -> {"timeout_s": int, "cleanup_cmd": str|None, "cleanup_timeout_s": int}. Reads cfg["gate"]; defaults timeout_s 2700, cleanup_cmd None, cleanup_timeout_s 300. cfg None -> orchestrator.pool.config(). A non-positive or non-int timeout_s falls back to the default. A target repo overrides via its own .orchestrator/pool.toml (ORCH_ROOT), no extra code needed.
- run_bounded(argv, *, cwd, timeout_s, input=None, kill_grace_s=KILL_GRACE_S) -> {"returncode": int|None, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "timed_out": bool, "duration_s": float}. Start the child with start_new_session=True (own process group). On timeout: os.killpg(pgid, SIGTERM), wait up to kill_grace_s, then os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL); ignore ProcessLookupError; collect whatever output exists; returncode None when timed_out.
- run_gate(worktree, *, script, task_id=None, cfg=None) -> {"returncode": int|None, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "timed_out": bool, "attempts": int, "timeouts": int}. Runs [str(script), worktree] with cwd=worktree and input "{}" (tests-green.sh reads stdin first and blocks without it) via run_bounded with settings(cfg)["timeout_s"]. On each timeout, in order: (1) the tree is already killed by run_bounded, (2) if cleanup_cmd is set, run it via run_bounded(["bash", "-c", cleanup_cmd], cwd=worktree, timeout_s=cleanup_timeout_s) and ignore its result, (3) notify (orchestrator.notify, e.g. notify.notify(...) or the same _deliver the daemon uses) with task_id, attempt number and timeout_s, (4) retry once. At most 2 attempts total. timed_out is True only when the last attempt timed out, and then returncode is None: a timeout is never success. A normal pass or red run returns on the first attempt with its real returncode and output.
- While an attempt runs, write STATE/"gates"/f"{key}.json" (key = task_id or a sanitized worktree basename) with {"task_id", "worktree", "pid", "started_at", "timeout_s"}; remove it in a finally block. STATE comes from orchestrator (from . import STATE); tests must point it at a temp dir (patch gate.STATE or the gates dir constant).
- running_gates(now=None, threshold=0.8) -> list of those registry entries whose elapsed (now - started_at) exceeds threshold * timeout_s, each with "elapsed_s" added. Unreadable files are skipped.

pool.toml: add a commented [gate] table (timeout_s = 2700, cleanup_cmd commented out with the luna example `xcrun simctl shutdown all`, cleanup_timeout_s = 300). Do not change any other section.

Tests (unittest.TestCase, tests/test_gate_timeout.py): pass cfg dicts explicitly, never read the live pool.toml; use tiny timeouts (e.g. 1 s) and kill_grace_s small; fake gate scripts written to a temp dir. The tree-kill test starts a script that spawns a sleeping child, records the child pid to a file, then sleeps; after run_bounded/run_gate returns, assert both processes are gone (os.kill(pid, 0) raises).
acceptance: tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_timeout_kills_process_tree passes: a fake gate that forks a sleeping child and sleeps past a 1 s timeout returns timed_out True and neither the parent nor the child pid is alive afterwards
tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_cleanup_command_runs_on_timeout passes: a configured cleanup_cmd (writes a marker file) runs after each timeout; with cleanup_cmd unset nothing extra runs

tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_timeout_retries_once passes: a gate that always hangs is attempted exactly twice, result timed_out True, returncode None, timeouts 2; a gate that hangs once then passes returns returncode 0, timed_out False, attempts 2

tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_fast_gate_unaffected passes: a fast passing gate and a fast failing gate each run once with their real returncode and output, no cleanup, no notify, and the .orchestrator/gates registry entry is removed

tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_settings_defaults_and_override passes: settings({}) gives timeout_s 2700, cleanup_cmd None, cleanup_timeout_s 300; a [gate] table overrides each; an invalid timeout_s falls back to 2700
tests/test_gate_timeout.py::test_running_gates_over_threshold passes: a registry entry past 80% of its timeout is listed with elapsed_s, one below is not

constraints.interface_contract: orchestrator/gate.py: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S=2700, KILL_GRACE_S=15, settings(cfg=None), run_bounded(argv,*,cwd,timeout_s,input=None,kill_grace_s=KILL_GRACE_S), run_gate(worktree,*,script,task_id=None,cfg=None), running_gates(now=None,threshold=0.8); see spec for return shapes
